implementationScope: Six approved pumpkin listings only: enrich canonical Nick’s Fall Fest and add Anderson Farms, Maize in the City, Miller Farms, The Patch in Kiowa and 7th Generation Farm. No merge or deployment authorization.
verificationMethod: Uses the supplied official-source research snapshots checked at the timestamps above. Implementing the records does not constitute a later source, ticket inventory or operating-status recheck.
editorialDecisions: Every approved pumpkin record remains in holiday and adds category pumpkin-patches. Existing non-pumpkin records and archive entries are unchanged.
Only event-geography labels Erie, Kiowa, Platteville and Louisville are added; no park datasets, park records or city guide pages are created.
Explicit remaining-date schedules use America/Denver offsets: -06:00 through October 31 and -07:00 on November 1. No generic season-to-daily recurrence expansion is used.

Anderson’s conflicting homepage closure banner is prominent and pumpkin.operatingStatus is conflicting. Occurrences preserve published hours only and availability remains unknown; the listing must not be treated as a confirmed operating recommendation.

Miller’s daily 9 a.m.–6 p.m. schedule is independently supported by the rendered homepage and the Labor Day-to-mid-November festival page. October 21–31 is conservatively within that published season. The exact November end is unknown, so series_end is null, seasonEndUnknown is true and editorialReviewThrough is October 31. dateEnd is the last enumerated October 31 closing time for expiry, not an assertion of the actual season end. No November occurrence is invented.
Nick is retail pumpkin selection; Maize is a stocked field with brought-in pumpkins. Neither claims vine picking.
The Patch checkout HTTP 403 is recorded as a research-access limitation, not proof the public checkout is broken. Official ticket landing URL is retained.
7th Generation pumpkin prices remain visibly undated. Its October 24 $11.37 single-ticket quote and sampled add-on totals are not generalized to all dates or carts.
Separate entry, pumpkin and activity costs and material warnings are provided in pumpkin.preview for short previews. costLabel never describes the whole paid-pumpkin outing as simply free.
Readable lastEntry labels identify gate, wagon, hayride and maze cutoffs separately from closing time; conflicting or unpublished last entry is not invented.
All occurrence availability values remain unknown. Booking links, price samples and a quantity dropdown are not evidence of live capacity or remaining tickets.

essentials: Pumpkin wagon stops at 5:30 p.m.; its line can close earlier on busy days. The field is unlit after dark. Monday/Wednesday gate entry ends at 4:30 p.m.

Online purchase is strongly recommended. Timed tickets allow a 30-minute entry window, then staying until closing; same-day reentry requires a wristband. If tickets sell out online they are also sold out at the gate.
Separate retail-only pumpkin sales need no festival admission, 10 a.m.–6 p.m. except Tuesdays; that route does not include field access.
Small maze trail is designed for ages 2–8; Mookie’s Play Yard is designed for children under 48 inches. Terror in the Corn is a separate haunted offering, not ordinary pumpkin admission.

Accessible wagon available on request at loading; regular festival access needs no special reservation. Accessible indoor stalls and portable toilets are available, but none are inside the maze. Wellness room has an adult changing table.
Dirt, gravel and uneven or muddy terrain; all-terrain stroller advised. Outside food allowed, no alcohol; no pets except ADA service animals.

Painting runs weekends; pony rides and mini-launch Friday–Sunday; paintball and escape room Thursday evening–Sunday. Confirm the day’s lineup. Face painting, escape room and food prices are variable or unpublished.
Campfire rentals are $150 small/$300 large for four hours; pavilions $100–$400. Reservations required and festival admission extra.
Tickets are generally final sale, including weather and personal-plan changes; remedies when the farm cancels are discretionary under its July 6, 2026 purchase policy.

Detailed admission pricing: Ages 4+: October 21–25 Mon/Wed/Thu $18 timed or $23 gate; Friday $25 timed or $35 anytime/gate; Saturday/Sunday $32 timed or $42 anytime/gate. October 26–30 Mon/Wed/Thu $13.50 timed/gate; Friday $18.75 timed or $26.25 anytime/gate. October 31 $16 timed or $21 anytime/gate. Closed Tuesdays. Ages 0–3 free, no ticket needed. Final taxes/fees unresolved.

Detailed pumpkin pricing and selection: Extra: current linked size chart lists itty bitty $3, small $5, medium $7, large $10, extra large $15 and jumbo $20. FAQ conflicts at $2–$12. The 30-acre field advertises 70+ varieties, without stock guarantees.

Detailed activities and prices: Included: nonhaunted 25-acre corn maze, pumpkin wagon, barrel train, trike track, jump pad, combine slide, low ropes, playgrounds/games, animal viewing and scheduled entertainment. Petting zoo $5; gem mining $8.50–$60; duck $2; paintball $8 one/$14 both; bear factory from $29.99; pony $10 or $14 with photo; pumpkin painting $10; mini-pumpkin launch $5 per bucket. Food and other extras cost more.
